title: Self-hosted media server or a managed live video service?
body: Teams building live features, from watch parties to tournament streams, either run an open source media server or buy a managed service. Which route did you take, and where did the work end up?

The [MediaMTX repository](https://github.com/bluenviron/mediamtx) describes a live media server and proxy supporting SRT, WebRTC, RTSP, RTMP and LL-HLS, among others. The [SRS site](https://ossrs.io/lts/en-us/) describes an open source realtime server supporting RTMP, WebRTC, HLS, HTTP-FLV, SRT and MPEG-DASH. On the managed side, the [Amazon IVS page](https://aws.amazon.com/ivs/) describes a hosted service for low-latency interactive live video.
Details we would like to hear: expected audience size, whether you needed sub-second delay, who handles transcoding and what monitoring you ended up building.
